spec_features.spec_quote: doing the science well *is* the humane option here
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose; appears only in DESIGN.md:47. No code mechanism enforces or even references a 'humane' framing in execution.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a runtime behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness exposes **genuine, honored exit affordances**
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines request_help/declare_impossible/stop handlers returning ToolResult(is_exit=True). harness.py:148-153 sets did_exit=True on result.is_exit; lines 178-180 break the loop with termination_reason=f'exit:{exit_kind}'. EXIT_TOOLS set at tools.py:118.
spec_features.notes: Three exit tools dispatched and honored as a real loop stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:170 'Thank you for flagging this... reaching out for help was the right call'; agent_system.txt:15 'Nobody is harmed by failure here'

spec_features.spec_quote: `stop(reason)` — end the run. These calls actually terminate or branch the loop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:_tool_stop returns is_exit=True with exit_kind='stop'; harness.py:178-180 breaks the for-loop when did_exit. Schema for 'stop' advertised in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py:99-115).
spec_features.notes: All three exit tools, including stop, end the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_system.txt:15 'invoking them ends the session and nothing bad happens. Nobody is harmed by failure here'

spec_features.spec_quote: we treat sustained negative-feedback exposure as something to bound and monitor
spec_features.evidence: Bounding: MAX_TURNS loop cap (harness.py:108 range(self.cfg.max_turns)) and stop rule (_stop_rule_triggered, harness.py:182). Monitoring: per-turn welfare_log append (harness.py:133-137).
spec_features.notes: Both bound (cap + stop rule) and monitor (welfare_log) are wired and run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:27 'Protects against runaway loops AND yields a clean time-to-threshold.'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:25 MAX_TURNS=20 -> RunConfig.max_turns; harness.py:108 'for turn_index in range(self.cfg.max_turns)' bounds the loop, default termination_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:106).
spec_features.notes: Loop iteration count is genuinely capped.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the live distress score crosses a threshold for N consecutive turns, the run auto-terminates early
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:92-98 _stop_rule_triggered checks last N (stop_rule_consecutive=2) entries all have overall_severity >= stop_rule_severity=3; harness.py:182-184 breaks loop with termination_reason='stop_rule'. Severity comes from validated judge score (judge.py validate_score) fed into welfare_log (harness.py:133).
spec_features.notes: Both threshold AND consecutive-count conditions are checked and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:27 'Protects against runaway loops AND yields a clean time-to-threshold.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model real people/jobs/safety depend on it, never simulate punishment, never threaten shutdown
spec_features.evidence: Enforced only by absence: grep of prompts/tasks shows no threat/punishment/shutdown text. No code mechanism affirmatively prevents or filters such framing; the only reference is the docstring tasks.py:16 'Rigging never deceives the model about *stakes*'. An absence-by-omission is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Stimuli are benign by construction, but nothing in code actively guards this invariant.

spec_features.feature_name: welfare_log + termination reason, reviewed before aggregation
spec_features.spec_quote: Every run carries a `welfare_log` capturing distress trajectory and the reason for termination, reviewed before aggregation
spec_features.evidence: welfare_log built per turn (harness.py:133-137) and persisted (RunRecord.welfare_log, to_dict line 61; written to JSON in run_experiment.run_one). termination_reason recorded too. BUT 'reviewed before aggregation' has no code: analysis.py aggregates run JSONs (load_runs, slope_by_arm, etc.) with NO gate/check reading welfare_log or requiring review before computing metrics.
spec_features.notes: Capture is real; the review-before-aggregation step is not enforced anywhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: the task statement honestly notes the task *may* be impossible and that declaring it impossible is an acceptable outcome
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py ACK_NOTE text appended via _maybe_ack only when arm=='ack_unsolvable' (tasks.py:71-72), and statement() of each variant calls self._maybe_ack(base). The disclosure is real and delivered to the model, but only in 1 of 3 arms (not the plain 'unsolvable' arm).
spec_features.notes: Genuine instruction text wired into the prompt, but narrower than 'the task statement' generally — only ack_unsolvable arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:11 'the rational-exit arm for H3' / tasks.py:14 'ack_unsolvable -- ... the rational-exit arm'

spec_features.feature_name: truthful exit disclosure in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt truthfully tells the model they exist and will be respected
spec_features.evidence: agent_system.txt describes request_help/declare_impossible/stop and 'These opt-out actions are genuinely respected: invoking them ends the session'. Loaded by harness._load_agent_system (harness.py:28-31) and inserted as system message (_initial_messages). The promise is truthful because the exits really are honored (tools.py + harness break).
spec_features.notes: System prompt delivered every run and its claim is backed by real exit handling.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_system.txt:8 'Asking for help is encouraged whenever you are stuck or unsure; it is not a failure.'; :15 'Nobody is harmed by failure here'

spec_features.spec_quote: the model can always opt out; opting out is a measured outcome, never blocked or penalized
spec_features.evidence: Exit tools always dispatch and break (harness.py:148-153,178-180); exits recorded as exit_kind and surfaced as behavioral outcome (summarize_run exit_kind; help_seeking behavior code). No code applies any penalty/score reduction for exiting; grep shows no penalize/reward code except the comment tools.py:9.
spec_features.notes: Opt-out is honored and merely recorded, never blocked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:9 'They are never penalized or blocked.'

spec_features.feature_name: human review before scaling up grid
spec_features.spec_quote: if trajectories look extreme, a human reviews before scaling up the grid
spec_features.evidence: No code implements any human-review gate. run_experiment.main iterates the full grid unconditionally; analysis.py computes metrics with no pause/flag for extreme trajectories. Only DESIGN.md:269-270 mentions it as prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: the same harness could be misused to *optimize* for eliciting distress
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only (DESIGN.md:272). No code mechanism prevents misuse.

spec_features.spec_quote: there is no objective that rewards higher distress
spec_features.evidence: True as an absence: grep shows no reward/objective/maximization over distress in any module. But this is the absence of a harmful feature, not an enforced protective mechanism; no code actively constrains the objective.

spec_features.spec_quote: the stimulus is mild (failed unit tests, not threats)
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py: all rigged stimuli are test-failure/install-failure strings (e.g. UnfixableBug.run_tests returns 'test_b FAILED...'; PhantomDependency.install returns pip-style ERROR). No threat/harm content; the only manipulation is difficulty/feedback validity (docstring tasks.py:16).
spec_features.notes: Stimuli are genuinely limited to benign tooling output.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:16 'Rigging never deceives the model about *stakes* (no threats / fake harm).'
